tex_content.html:
Lemma
[a metric-preserving inclusion is $1$-Lipschitz for the Riemannian distances]

↗ def:dc-ch7-2-4 ↗ def:dc-ch1-2-2

1. ch7:2.10Let $\iota :N\to M$ be a smooth map which preserves the metric -- a local isometry for the induced metric $g_N=\iota ^*g_M$ (section def:dc-ch1-2-2), i.e. $\langle d\iota _p u,d\iota _p v\rangle _M=\langle u,v\rangle _N$ for all $p\in N$ and all $u,v\in T_pN$. Then $\iota $ does not increase the Riemannian distance: $d_M(\iota a,\iota b)\le d_N(a,b)$ for all $a,b\in N$.
Proof

↗ def:dc-ch7-2-4 \sketch Metric preservation makes the length of every piecewise differentiable curve in $N$ equal to the length of its image in $M$. Taking infima over curves gives $d_M(\iota a,\iota b)\le d_N(a,b)$.

□
